analysis: COHORT/SITE confound probe (non-ADD): Kerchner vs Poston
design: non-ADD subset (30) -> Cohort LevelMap Kerchner (7, positive) vs Poston (20, negative); 3 other-site samples (ADRC/PUC=2, PUC only=1) DROPPED; n=27. Elastic net, stratified 5-fold x 5-repeat, in-fold scaling, class_weight balanced, target=individuals.

null_read.verdict: SITE AUC COLLAPSES to its null — the on-Cohort correction removed detectable within-non-ADD site structure. This does NOT clear the ADD result: ADD is single-cohort, so its correction was EXTRAPOLATED, not estimated (finding 0004).

feature_overlap_with_add_classifier.note: High overlap => the ADD signal and the site signal ride on the same proteins (damning for a disease interpretation). Low overlap is NOT exoneration: EN keeps one of a correlated cluster, so the two minimal-optimal sets can pick different members of the same underlying structure.

caveats: EXPLORATORY: tiny n (7 Kerchner positives), imbalanced; a bounded probe, not a powered analysis. Wide CIs.

The matrix is ALREADY batch-corrected on Cohort (finding 0004). A null-level site AUC means the correction removed detectable within-nonADD site structure — it does NOT clear the ADD result (ADD single-cohort => correction extrapolated, not estimated).
An above-null site AUC means residual site structure survives correction where it was estimable — evidence the ADD separation is substantially site.
Low feature overlap is NOT exoneration (EN keeps one of a correlated cluster; the two minimal-optimal sets can pick different members of the same structure).
